summary: Three control-plane scale/resilience fixes for larger or partially-unreachable fleets. Heartbeat (node_registry.go) previously mTLS-probed nodes without a live control connection one at a time, so a handful of unreachable nodes could blow an entire sweep past the heartbeat interval; probing now runs through a bounded worker pool (heartbeatProbeConcurrency = 16) under a per-sweep budget (heartbeatSweepBudget = 30s) via new probeNodesConcurrently, while DB reconciliation/writes stay serial for the single-writer sqlite store. NodeRegistry.List previously called Get(...,1000,0,...) once, silently truncating the fleet at 1000 adopted nodes and cascading into the operator Nodes list, Scan adoption dedup, and Heartbeat itself; it now pages through the table in nodeListPageSize (500) chunks until exhausted. control_server.go now fails fast when a node's control channel drops mid-command: pending requests are tracked with their owning nodeID (pendingReq), and on disconnect failPending(nodeID) delivers a nil frame to every waiter bound to that node so SendRequest returns the new ErrNodeDisconnected immediately instead of hanging to controlRequestTimeout (30s); node_proxy.go maps it to the same 404 "node is not connected" as ErrNodeOffline. Idempotency keys for tunneled writes were not implemented in this change (would need node-side dedup support in mymatasan), so a non-idempotent write in flight at disconnect time has an unknown outcome and is not automatically retried.
compatibility: Backward compatible, no config or schema changes. Behavior for a fully healthy, small fleet is unchanged (concurrency and pagination are internal implementation details); the effects only become visible at larger fleet sizes (>1000 adopted nodes now correctly enumerated) or when nodes are unreachable/disconnecting (sweeps no longer stall, tunneled commands fail in ~seconds instead of up to 30s). Operators relying on a tunneled write silently succeeding despite a mid-flight disconnect should note the outcome is now surfaced as an error rather than a hang, but is still not auto-retried — verify node state before resending a non-idempotent command (e.g. settings writes, wipe).
